result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.has_eulerian_path()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check whether the graph has an Eulerian path. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L52050-L52109){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.has_eulerian_path(source=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Has Eulerian path](/assets/graphs/has-eulerian-path.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: the house of Santa Claus, a square with both diagonals and a roof; badges give each node's degree and only the bottom corners D and E are odd (outlined), so one stroke can draw it and has_eulerian_path() returns True. Right: without the roof (dashed), all four corners have degree 3 (shown in the accent color), so has_eulerian_path() returns False." width="100%"} Returns `True` if some trail uses every edge exactly once: either a closed circuit (`is_eulerian()`) or an open path between two nodes (`is_semieulerian()`). With `source=`, it checks for such a trail starting at that node, which for an open path means the node must be one of the two ends (on an undirected graph, an odd-degree node; on a directed graph, the node with one more out-edge than in-edges). Isolated nodes are ignored, as in `is_eulerian()`. NetworkX instead requires the whole graph to be connected, so results differ only for graphs with isolated nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optionally require the path to start here, as an integer ID or a string label. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if an Eulerian path exists (from `source=`, if given). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A path graph can be traced end to end, but only from one of its ends: ::: {#6ceb7227 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4) path.has_eulerian_path(), path.has_eulerian_path(source=1), path.has_eulerian_path(source=2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, True, False) ``` ::: ::: A star with three leaves has four odd nodes, so no single stroke covers it: ::: {#bb2d5e1f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_star_graph(4).has_eulerian_path() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
